one_liner: Mozilla's Firefox JavaScript and WebAssembly engine, embeddable through the C++ JSAPI; its JIT tiers score about 16x QuickJS on v8-v7.
what_it_does: SpiderMonkey is the JavaScript and WebAssembly engine inside Firefox; its source lives under js/src in the Firefox monorepo and builds standalone as libmozjs (shared or static) plus the js shell. A C++ host creates a JSContext, creates a global object populated with JS_InitStandardClasses, runs code with JS::Evaluate and exposes native functions as JSNative callbacks. It is not a drop-in for QuickJS or Duktape: the API is C++ only, needs precise GC rooting (JS::Rooted, trace hooks) and changes between releases, so Mozilla tells embedders to track an ESR branch (ESR 140 in the current embedding guide).
how_it_is_fast: Tiered execution: a C++ interpreter, then a baseline interpreter and baseline JIT that attach inline caches expressed in CacheIR, then the Warp optimizing tier, where WarpOracle snapshots the CacheIR stubs the baseline ICs collected and WarpBuilder turns bytecode into MIR off the main thread for the Ion backend (register allocation, native code). A generational GC with a nursery and the Irregexp regular-expression engine (js/src/irregexp) cover the allocation- and RegExp-heavy tests. The 16x gap over QuickJS and Duktape is the JIT-versus-interpreter gap; with --disable-jit or on targets without a JIT backend SpiderMonkey runs on its interpreters, optionally the Portable Baseline Interpreter, which interprets CacheIR without generating code.
when_to_use: A C++ host that runs long or compute-heavy scripts and needs JIT throughput: 19137 vs QuickJS 1217 on Ubuntu, with per-test gains of 16-22x on Richards, DeltaBlue, Crypto, RayTrace, EarleyBoyer and RegExp (Splay 6.9x, NavierStokes 11x; derived from page data).

Products that want an engine with a long-lived API: Mozilla publishes yearly ESR branches with security backports and recommends embedders track them; Linux distributions package mozjs-140, so hosts there can skip the source build.

Hosts on x86, x86-64, ARM, AArch64, MIPS64, LoongArch64 or RISC-V64 (the JIT is on by default for these in js/moz.configure), or on JIT-less targets such as wasm32-wasi, where the Portable Baseline Interpreter still gives IC-based speed-ups without codegen.
Multi-threaded hosts that can give each thread its own JSContext tied to the main runtime (worker.cpp example) and share compiled scripts across threads with Stencils (stencils.cpp).

MPL-2.0 is acceptable: SpiderMonkey sources carry per-file MPL 2.0 headers (e.g. js/src/jsapi.h), so a proprietary host can link the library while changes to SpiderMonkey's own files stay open; the repository LICENSE points to toolkit/content/license.html for bundled third-party licences.
when_not_to_use: Peak throughput: V8 scores 48107 vs 19137 on Ubuntu (about 2.5x) and wins every sub-test; JavaScriptCore scores 45928 in the same run.

Small footprint: the Ubuntu shell is 40.8 MB vs about 1 MB for QuickJS and 370 KB for Duktape, so score per MB is 468 vs 1190 and 1352; the build drags in the Firefox tree, Rust, Python-driven configure and ICU.
Short scripts or many cold starts: the v8-v7 harness throws away a 1 s warm-up per test, so JIT warm-up cost is not in the measured score and the 16x does not describe one-shot snippets.

Untrusted code where JIT attack surface matters: JIT miscompilation CVEs keep landing (CVE-2026-10702, a JIT type confusion fixed in Firefox 151.0.3, per search snippets); build with --disable-jit or force the portable baseline interpreter if runtime codegen is not allowed.
Teams that cannot absorb API churn: master breaks the embedding API often, and moving between ESRs needs the migration guide.

integration.form: shared lib (libmozjs-<version>) or static lib built from js/src of the Firefox tree, plus the js shell; distro packages (mozjs-140) on Linux
integration.dependencies: Rust toolchain (1.82+ for ESR 140), GNU Make, Python (mach/configure), zlib, libffi, ICU 76.1+ (bundled copy by default); mozglue if jemalloc is left enabled
integration.min_toolchain: Current main forces -std=gnu++20 and requires clang 19+ (clang-cl on Windows) or GCC 11.1+; the ESR 140 embedding guide asks for a C++17 compiler and Rust 1.82
integration.platforms: JIT backends for x86, x86-64, ARM, AArch64, MIPS64, LoongArch64 and RISC-V64; interpreter-only (optionally Portable Baseline Interpreter) elsewhere, including wasm32-wasi; Mozilla ships prebuilt jsshell zips for Linux x86-64, Windows x64 and macOS
integration.thread_safety: A JSContext is single-threaded; extra threads create their own JSContext with the main JSRuntime as parent, initialize self-hosted code and create their own global (worker.cpp). The engine uses helper threads for off-thread Warp compilation and GC.

gotchas: Harness: v8-v7 base.js runs each of the 10 tests for a 1 s discarded warm-up plus at least 1 s timed (and at least 32 iterations), so 20 s is a floor every JIT engine hits; the record's '20 s vs QuickJS 37 s vs Duktape 70 s' wall time is not a speed ratio, and each engine runs once per day with no variance. The macOS total of 134.9 MB is a 67.5 MB exe (jsshell-mac.zip, which spidermonkey-build uses for both x86_64 and aarch64) plus another 67.5 MB counted as 'Dll size'; the cause is not documented.

Stale binary: js-engine-setup installs the latest ahaoboy/spidermonkey-build release, but that repo's daily refresh workflow is disabled by GitHub after 60 days without repository activity, so the measured jsshell is frozen at 147.0 while Firefox main is at 159.0a1; it predates later JIT fixes such as CVE-2026-10702 (fixed in 151.0.3) and any performance work since.

Build the library for embedding with --disable-jemalloc (or link the matching mozglue): the default browser-oriented jemalloc configuration leads to crashes when memory allocated by jemalloc is freed by the system allocator, per the embedding guide.

Every GC thing held across calls must be rooted (JS::Rooted, or traced from your own structures as in tracing.cpp). The spidermonkey-embedding-examples default branch is still esr102; use the esr140 branch for the current ESR.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick SpiderMonkey over QuickJS, Duktape or Escargot when throughput on long-running scripts matters more than a 40 MB footprint and a heavy build, and over V8 when you want ESR branches with year-long API stability under MPL-2.0; V8 is 2.5x faster here, and ChakraCore matches its score (19392 vs 19137 on Ubuntu) at about half the size but has had no tagged release since 2020.
verified_claims_summary: ahaoboy/js-engine-benchmark runs the v8-v7 suite (8 suites, geometric-mean Score) once per engine per day on GitHub-hosted ubuntu, macos-arm64 and windows runners (CPU not stated); in the 10/5/2026 snapshot Mozilla's prebuilt jsshell 147.0 scored 19137 / 25455 / 19049 against QuickJS 2026-06-04 at 1217 / 1761 / 1067 (about 15.7x, 14.5x and 17.9x, derived from page data) and Duktape at 489 / 905 / 371. SpiderMonkey uses Mozilla's release-build flags; QuickJS and Duktape come from the suite owner's build repos with flags not stated on the page.
status_note: Actively developed in the Firefox tree (main at 159.0a1) with ESR branches for embedders; MPL-2.0 and usable as libmozjs from source or distro packages, but the measured shell is a frozen 147.0 build and the engine is heavy to build and integrate.
